newsitem.title: UK: Press Digest - Evening Standard - March 7.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Evening Standard - March 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- NOW BLAIR DARES TO SPEAK OF VICTORY

The latest Gallup poll for the Daily Telegraph has put Labour 26 percent ahead of the Tories, an unprecedented lead in the closing months before polling day. In an interview with the Glasgwow Herald, Labour leader Tony Blair commented "I acknowledge we are well-placed, but I take absolutely noting for granted, not even now."
SET-TOP BOXES DEAL STIRS UP DIGITAL WAR

Cable companies including Telewest have signed a deal with General Instrument of the US, in an attempt to gain the advantage over BSkyB in supplying set-top boxes for multi-channel digital TV and information services.

The Chancellor Kenneth Clarke, currently on a flying visit to Hong Kong, has said that he will not 'start messing around' with monetary policy in the months before the General Election, affirming that economics and not politics would determine the direction of interest rates.
HOW CROCKFORDS LANDED IN THE PLONK
Garry Nesbitt, the chairman of casinos group Capital Corporation, was, it is believed, under pressure to resign following a meeting of non-executive directors last September.
An investigation by Network Security into Capital's Crockfords casino had been highly critical of Nesbitt's wine purchasing.
However, when the 181m stg hostile bid from London Clubs International materialised in February, the demand for Nesbitt to go was apparently called off.
The company has denied that the resignation of Nesbitt was sought by directors.
